bandReport.notes: Band b2 = pages p08-p14, questions 61-100 (40 questions); the paper ends at Q100 on p14. SEAM CHECK BEFORE: opened p07 (owned by band b1) - it carries Q54-Q60, and Q60 is complete there with all four options, so nothing straddles the p07/p08 boundary and Q61 starts clean at the top of p08. SEAM CHECK AFTER: p14 is the last page of the booklet, Q100 is complete with all four options, nothing follows it. NO Directions / 'Consider the following for the next N items' shared-stimulus blocks appear anywhere in p08-p14, so this band contains no sets and no question carries context/setLabel. (Q97 and Q99 each print a 'Consider the following statements' list, but those lists belong to that single question and are transcribed inside its own stem - they are not shared stimulus.) FIGURES: 9 questions carry a printed diagram and are flagged hasFigure - Q90, Q91, Q92 (p12), Q93, Q94, Q95, Q96 (p13), Q97, Q98 (p14). Every figureNote was written after cropping that region at 2.6-3.2x and reading it; none of the figure content is described in a stem. MISPRINT / ODDITY flagged: Q91 needed an invented subtopic (see its flags). Q94's printed figure marks x twice at C and y at D but prints NO arc or label at B even though the stem says BD bisects angle B - noted in its figureNote for the crop operator, stem left as printed. Q73 mixes units as printed (ball radius in cm, pipe length 14 m, options in square cm) - transcribed verbatim, not a transcription error. Q100's options are printed without any unit, as shown. Nothing in this band was illegible: every ambiguous glyph (Q61/Q79/Q82/Q90 exponents and denominators, Q66/Q78/Q80/Q91/Q100 option sets, Q69's option signs) was re-cropped at 3-5x and read again before transcription. Raised middle dots in the source decimals (4.5, 5.5, 3.5, 31.25 etc.) were transcribed as full stops per the brief.

questions.stem: In the figure given below, AC is parallel to ED and AB = DE = 5 cm and BC = 7 cm. What is the area ABDE : area BDE : area BCD equal to ?
questions.figureNote: Zig-zag figure between two horizontal parallel lines, in the right column below the stem. On the lower line, left to right: A, then B, then C, with the segment A to B labelled '5 cm' and the segment B to C labelled '7 cm'. On the upper line, left to right: E then D, with the segment E to D labelled '5 cm'. E sits above a point between A and B; D sits above a point between B and C, close to B's side. Drawn segments are A to E, E to B, B to D, D to C, the upper segment E to D, and the whole lower line A to B to C — giving triangle AEB on the left, triangle EBD in the middle (apex down at B) and triangle BDC on the right. No angle marks, no right angles, no other measurements printed.

questions.stem: In the figure given below, PQRS is a parallelogram. PA bisects angle P and SA bisects angle S. What is angle PAS equal to ?
questions.figureNote: Parallelogram drawn as a wide slanted quadrilateral, vertices labelled outside: P at top-left, Q at top-right, S at bottom-left, R at bottom-right (so PQ is the top side, SR the bottom side, PS the short left side, QR the short right side). A point A is marked inside the parallelogram, in the left part, roughly level with the middle of side PS and about a third of the way across. Two segments are drawn: P to A and S to A, forming triangle PAS. No angle arcs, no tick marks and no measurements are printed on the figure. Sits between the stem and the options in the left column.

questions.stem: In the figure given below, \( \angle A = 80^\circ \) and \( \angle ABC = 60^\circ \). BD and CD bisect angles B and C respectively. What are the values of x and y respectively ?
questions.figureNote: Wide scalene triangle, apex A at top (left of centre), B at bottom-left, C at bottom-right. A point D is marked inside the triangle, below A and left of centre; segments B to D and D to C are drawn. At D, an arc across the angle BDC is labelled 'y' with a degree sign. At C two arcs are drawn with the vertex at C, one above the other: the upper arc spans the angle between CA and CD and is labelled 'x' with a degree sign, the lower arc spans the angle between CD and CB and is also labelled 'x' with a degree sign. NOTE for the crop operator: the printed figure carries NO arc or label at B, even though the stem says BD bisects angle B — do not crop this out as if it were missing ink; it is simply not printed. No side lengths are shown. Sits between the stem and the options in the left column.

questions.stem: In the figure given below, PQR is a non-isosceles right-angled triangle, right angled at Q. If LM and QT are parallel and QT = PT, then what is \( \angle RLM \) equal to ?
questions.figureNote: Right-angled triangle standing on its base: P at the top-left, Q at the bottom-left, R at the bottom-right. Side PQ is the near-vertical left side, QR the horizontal base, PR the hypotenuse sloping down from P to R. A small square right-angle mark is drawn inside the triangle at Q. On the hypotenuse PR two points are marked, T higher up (roughly the midpoint of PR, its label to the right of the line) and M lower down (between T and R, label to the right). On the base QR one point L is marked, between Q and R and roughly below T. Two internal segments are drawn: Q to T, and L to M. They appear parallel to each other. No angle arcs, no tick marks and no measurements are printed. Sits between the stem and the options at the top of the right column.

questions.stem: In the figure given below, PQ is parallel to RS and PR is parallel to QS. If \( \angle LPR = 35^\circ \) and \( \angle UST = 70^\circ \), then what is \( \angle MPQ \) equal to ?
questions.figureNote: Five full straight lines, every one drawn with an arrowhead at BOTH ends (no segments). Four of them form a slanted parallelogram whose corners, reading round, are P at the top-left, Q at the right, S at the bottom and R at the left. The two lines PQ and RS run from upper-left down to lower-right and are parallel; the two lines PR and QS run steeply from top down to bottom and are parallel. Every side is extended past both corners to its arrowheads. Marked dots on the extensions: U lies on line RS beyond S (to the lower right of S), and T lies on line QS beyond S (below S). The fifth line is a separate transversal that crosses the parallelogram only at the corner P, running from lower-left to upper-right: L is a marked dot on it below and left of P, M is a marked dot on it above and right of P, so L, P and M are collinear. No angle arcs and no measurements are printed anywhere on the figure. Sits between the stem and the options in the right column; crop must include all eight letters L, P, M, R, Q, S, U, T and every arrowhead.

questions.stem:
In the figure given below, ABC is a triangle with AB = BC and D is an interior point of the triangle ABC such that \( \angle DAC = \angle DCA \).

Consider the following statements :

1. Triangle ADC is an isosceles triangle.

2. D is the centroid of the triangle ABC.

3. Triangle ABD is congruent to the triangle CBD.

Which of the above statements are correct ?
questions.figureNote: Triangle standing on a horizontal base, apex B at the top (label above the apex), A at the bottom-left and C at the bottom-right. A point D is marked inside the triangle, below B and slightly right of the vertical through B, its label printed just under the point. Three internal-looking segments are drawn from D: a short near-vertical segment B to D, and two segments D to A and D to C, so that triangle ADC sits inside triangle ABC sharing the base AC. No angle arcs, no tick marks, no measurements printed. The figure sits between the opening sentence of the stem and the 'Consider the following statements' list, in the left column — the crop must contain the figure only, not the surrounding text.

questions.stem: In the figure given below, M is the mid-point of AB and \( \angle DAB = \angle CBA \) and \( \angle AMC = \angle BMD \). Then the triangle ADM is congruent to the triangle BCM by
questions.figureNote: Bow-tie / hourglass figure between two horizontal lines. On the upper line, C at the left end and D at the right end, joined by the segment CD; the upper line is shorter than the lower one. On the lower line, A at the left end, M in the middle and B at the right end, drawn as the single segment A to B with M marked on it. Eight straight segments in all: CD across the top, AB along the bottom, then C to A, C to M, C to B, D to A, D to M and D to B — so the two long diagonals C-to-B and D-to-A cross near the centre, and the two segments C-to-M and D-to-M meet at M to form a V with its point at M. No angle arcs, no tick marks and no measurements are printed. Sits between the stem and the options in the left column.
